item.title: Yamal breaks Mbappe’s record as UCL’s highest-scoring teenager [See top 5]
item.description: Barcelona winger Lamine Yamal has surpassed Real Madrid forward Kylian Mbappé to become the highest-scoring teenager in UEFA Champions League history. The 19-year-old set the new record after scoring in Barcelona’s 3-0 victory over Aston Villa on Tuesday. Yamal capitalised on a defensive error by Villa in the seventh minute at Spotify Camp Nou, curling the ball beyond goalkeeper Zion Suzuki to register his 14th Champions League goal. The goal moved him past Mbappé, who previously held the teenage scoring record with 13 goals in the competition. Although the France international has scored 72 Champions League goals overall, Yamal has now claimed the record after just 37 appearances in Europe’s premier club competition. The Spain international has also established several other milestones in the tournament, including becoming the youngest player to start a Champions League match proper. Yamal achieved that feat at the age of 16 years and 83 days when he made his full European debut against FC Porto. His latest achievement comes after an impressive showing at the 2026 Ballon d’Or awards, where he finished third behind Bayern Munich striker Harry Kane and Mbappé. The Barcelona youngster has also enjoyed a productive start to the new season, recording 13 goals and 11 assists in 15 appearances across all competitions. item.title: FG Secured 2,512 Terrorism Convictions In Nine Years — NSA
item.description: Following the conclusion of the 11th phase of terrorism trials at the Federal High Court, Abuja, the federal government said it has secured a total of 2,512 convictions in terrorism-related cases over nine years. National Coordinator of the National Counter Terrorism Centre, Office of the National Security Adviser, Major General Adamu Laka, disclosed this during a press briefing in Abuja on Tuesday. According to him, the latest phase, conducted in October 2026, recorded 791 additional convictions out of 1,069 cases handled across 10 courts. He said the trials demonstrated the government’s commitment to combating terrorism, holding perpetrators and their financiers accountable, and strengthening the administration of justice while upholding the rule of law and the fundamental rights of defendants. The National Coordinator said the judgment showed the seriousness with which Nigeria’s justice system addresses terrorism and affirms that perpetrators, regardless of affiliation, were accountable under the law when criminal responsibility was established beyond reasonable doubt. Major General Laka revealed that among the significant outcomes of this phase was the conviction and sentencing to death of Suleiman Abu, in the case of the Federal Republic of Nigeria versus Suleiman Abu. He said the Federal High Court found him guilty of Boko Haram membership and participation in terrorist attacks on military facilities and civilians, resulting in deaths and serious injuries. item.title: Soludo seeks pharmacists’ support against fake drugs
item.description: By Steve Oko Anambra State Governor, Prof. Chukwuma Soludo, has called for stronger collaboration with the Pharmaceutical Society of Nigeria (PSN) to tackle fake drugs, improve healthcare delivery and position the state as a major pharmaceutical hub. Soludo made the call while declaring open the 99th Annual National Conference of the PSN, tagged Ijele 2026, in Awka. Speaking on the theme, “One Health, One Pharmacy: Bridging Knowledge, Practice and Policy for National Impact,” the governor described pharmacists as indispensable partners in building an efficient and sustainable healthcare system. He urged the professional body to work with his administration to enforce standards and sanitise the pharmaceutical sector, particularly by tackling counterfeit medicines and illegal operators posing as licensed pharmacies. Soludo said his administration was consolidating Anambra’s position as a pharmaceutical hub through the development of a pharmaceutical hub in Oba and a Coordinated Wholesale Centre, which he said was expected to be completed early next year. The governor also highlighted his administration’s investments in education and healthcare, saying the provision of free education from kindergarten to secondary school had reduced the state’s out-of-school children rate to 0.25 per cent, which he described as the lowest in the country. He further disclosed that the state had strengthened its primary healthcare system, provided free antenatal services to more than 250,000 beneficiaries and conducted over 950 free caesarean operations for expectant mothers. Earlier, PSN President, Pharm. Ayuba Tanko Ibrahim, commended Soludo for his support for the pharmaceutical profession. Ibrahim described Anambra’s hosting of the conference as the fulfilment of a longstanding commitment and praised the governor’s leadership and vision. He said the conference provided an opportunity to deepen cooperation between the pharmaceutical profession and government towards improving healthcare delivery. item.title: Four Nigerian-Americans win US midterm elections
item.description: Four Nigerian-Americans have won elective positions in the November 3 midterm elections in the United States, while the outcome of another candidate, Segun Adeyina, remained pending in Georgia as votes were being counted. Jawando. Photo: Wusa9 The winners are Will Jawando, Junior Ezeonu, Oye Owolewa and Carol Kazeem, who secured positions in local government and state legislatures across Maryland, Texas, Washington, DC, and Pennsylvania. In Maryland, Jawando, the Democratic candidate, won the race for Montgomery County executive, defeating Republican candidate Esther Wells. Results published by NBC Washington on Wednesday showed Jawando polling 237,383 votes, representing 78.15 per cent, against Wells’s 66,383 votes, or 21.85 per cent, with 72 per cent of the expected votes counted. READ ALSO; US Midterms: Democrats take control of US Congress as voters reject Trump’s Republicans Jawando, who previously served on the Montgomery County Council, is the son of a Nigerian father and an American mother. His Nigerian heritage and political career have featured in reports by The Baltimore Banner and The Washington Post. In Texas, 27-year-old Ezeonu secured a seat in the state House of Representatives for District 101. He had defeated incumbent Chris Turner in the Democratic primary and was the only candidate on the ballot for the November general election after no Republican entered the race. According to his campaign biography, Ezeonu was born in Onitsha, Anambra State, and moved to Texas at the age of two. He was elected to the Grand Prairie City Council in 2021 and later became the city’s youngest mayor pro tempore. Oye Owolewa. Photo: Instagram (@repoyedc) In Washington, DC, Owolewa, the Democratic candidate, won an at-large seat on the District of Columbia Council. Local publication, The 51st, reported that Owolewa secured 69 per cent of the vote, against 21 per cent recorded by independent candidate Elissa Silverman. Owolewa, a pharmacist and son of Nigerian immigrants from Kwara and Osun states, previously served as the District’s elected shadow representative. The position allows its holder to advocate for Washington, DC, statehood but does not confer voting rights in the US Congress. Meanwhile, Kazeem, also a Democrat, retained her seat in the Pennsylvania House of Representatives, representing District 159. The result of Adeyina’s contest in Georgia had yet to be called as of Wednesday, with votes still being counted. item.title: ‘Good Job’, Trump Reacts To Democrats’ Victory, Says Iran War Played Role In Midterm Defeat
item.description: US President Donald Trump had rare praise for rival Democrats on Tuesday, saying they had done a “good job” after they routed his Republican Party in the midterm elections. “I think the Democrats did a good job. I really do. I think they did a good job. They fought hard,” Trump told Fox News, adding that there was a “mood in the air” and that “I shouldn’t feel guilty.” President Donald Trump said he would accept the results of US midterm elections — but quickly sought to shift the blame for the historic rout to his fellow Republicans. Time and again on the campaign trail, the 80-year-old told Republicans to “pretend I’m on the ballot.” That may have been exactly the problem, as voters put Democrats in control of the House and Senate. But Trump has never been one to take the blame, and in his first reaction to the election results Tuesday, he insisted that the Republican Party would have won in a “landslide” if he had actually been running. “I wasn’t on the Ballot and if I was, we would have won IN A LANDSLIDE! Thank you for your attention to this matter,” Trump said in a post on his Truth Social platform. Democratic US Senate candidate James Talarico celebrates with supporters after winning the Texas race during a midterm election night watch party at the Long Center for the Performing Arts in Austin, Texas, on November 3, 2026. Dismissing speculation about whether he would repeat his refusal to accept his 2020 presidential election loss to Joe Biden, Trump later took a conciliatory tone with The New York Times. “I am absolutely willing to accept those results,” he told The New York Times. “We’ll work with the Democrats, and we’ll, you know, look forward to working with them. We’ll probably work something out.” But Trump later gave a hint of what he really intended to do to Democratic attempts at legislating, posting a picture of his trademark red MAGA baseball hat with the single word: “VETO.” There was a bunker mentality in the White House as Trump and his top cabinet members watched the bruising results come in at a reception in the lavish East Room. “The White House mood is defiant,” a White House official told AFP. Some White House staffers dined on take-out from US chain restaurant The Cheesecake Factory — a dig at Democratic former president Barack Obama, who had said Trump’s White House renovations were “looking like Saddam Hussein opened a Cheesecake Factory.” Supporters cheer as Democrat senatorial candidate Roy Cooper speaks during an election night event in Raleigh, North Carolina on November 3, 2026. ‘Buckle Up’ A White House official questioned the quality of Republican candidates for the House and Senate. item.title: Dollar to Naira exchange rate today, November 4, 2026
item.description: The dollar-to-naira exchange rate remains a major focus for businesses, importers and Nigerians seeking to meet their foreign exchange needs on Wednesday, November 4, 2026. The Nigerian naira trades against the US dollar at different rates across the Nigerian Foreign Exchange Market (NFEM) and the parallel market, also known as the black market. The NFEM rate reflects transactions in the official foreign exchange market, while the parallel market rate is influenced by demand and supply among independent currency dealers. As of Wednesday morning, the dollar is quoted at approximately ₦1,380 for buying and ₦1,390 for selling in the parallel market. The latest reported official NFEM rate is approximately ₦1,346.43 per dollar, based on the November 3 market publication. In the parallel market, Bureau De Change operators offer different rates depending on location, dollar availability and transaction volume. The quoted buying and selling rates are therefore indicative and may change throughout the day. At the prevailing rates, $100 is worth approximately ₦134,643 at the official market rate and ₦139,000 at the parallel-market selling rate. The difference between the official and parallel-market selling rates is approximately ₦43.57 per dollar. Meanwhile, the naira’s performance in the official market remains influenced by foreign exchange supply, demand from importers and other market participants, and liquidity conditions. Nigerians are advised to confirm prevailing rates with their banks and authorised Bureau De Change operators before conducting foreign exchange transactions, as rates may fluctuate during the day. item.title: Atiku to flag off ADC presidential campaign in Sokoto
item.description: By Musa Ubandawaki, Sokoto Former Vice-President Atiku Abubakar, presidential candidate of the African Democratic Congress (ADC), is expected to visit Sokoto on Wednesday, November 4, 2026, to flag off the party’s presidential campaign activities in the state ahead of the 2027 general elections. Atiku is scheduled to arrive at the Sultan Abubakar III International Airport, Sokoto, at 9 a.m., where party supporters, political associates and members of the public are expected to receive him. The Coordinator of the Sokoto State ADC Presidential Campaign Council, Senator Ibrahim Lamido, disclosed this in a statement made available to journalists. According to the statement, the visit is part of the party’s efforts to strengthen its grassroots structures and consolidate support ahead of the 2027 presidential election. It called on party members, supporters and well-meaning residents to turn out in large numbers to welcome the ADC presidential candidate. The statement said the visit would also feature the flag-off of the party’s presidential campaign in Sokoto State at its secretariat, located at No. 1, Ilorin Road, Sokoto. The event is expected to attract party leaders, elected and appointed political office holders, local government and ward executives, mobilisation coordinators, support groups and other stakeholders. Lamido said local government and ward executives had been directed to activate their political structures and mobilise members and supporters across the state. Women and youth organisations, as well as affiliated support groups, were also urged to intensify grassroots mobilisation and participate actively in the event. The campaign council further called on mobilisation coordinators to ensure effective coordination among the party’s structures to guarantee a successful reception and campaign flag-off. Atiku’s visit comes amid increasing political activities and realignments ahead of the 2027 general elections, as political parties step up efforts to expand their support bases. The statement, however, did not provide further details of the presidential candidate’s engagements during the visit. item.title: Sanusi credits Tinubu for rescuing Nigeria’s economy from brink
item.description: The Emir of Kano, Muhammadu Sanusi II, has said President Bola Tinubu deserves credit for bringing Nigeria’s economy back from the brink, citing improvements in economic growth, inflation, foreign reserves and export diversification. Sanusi, however, cautioned that significant economic challenges remain, saying the country must sustain its current growth trajectory to achieve lasting stability. The former Governor of the Central Bank of Nigeria (CBN) spoke on Tuesday at the Oxford Global Think Tank conference convened by Arunma Oteh. “I’m not a fan of politicians, but we need to give credit to President Tinubu’s administration for bringing us back from the brink,” he said. Sanusi cited the country’s economic growth of 4.48 per cent in the second quarter of 2026, describing it as an improvement over the average performance recorded during the administration of former President Muhammadu Buhari. “GDP in Q2 2026 was at 4.48 percent. It’s not as high as it was under the Yar’Adua/Jonathan government, but during the Buhari years, the economy grew by 0.9 percent. Today it’s at 4.5 percent. That’s progress,” he said. He also highlighted the decline in inflation from about 30 per cent to 14.6 per cent, noting that it was projected to fall further to 12.5 per cent by the end of the year. On economic growth and living standards, the emir said Nigeria’s gross domestic product (GDP) per capita, measured in dollar terms, had increased by 47 per cent since 2023. He expressed optimism that sustaining the current pace of growth could restore the country’s GDP per capita to its 2005 level by the end of next year. “If we continue at this rate, by the end of next year, GDP per capita will be back to where it was in 2005,” he said. Sanusi also pointed to Nigeria’s foreign reserves, which he put at $55 billion, but warned that a substantial portion of the inflows was driven by foreign portfolio investments, which could be volatile. “Our reserves are at $55 billion, and yes, a lot of it is driven by portfolio flows, which are volatile,” he said. He attributed the continued inflows partly to high oil prices amid the conflict in the Strait of Hormuz and attractive returns available to investors in Nigeria. On export diversification, Sanusi said 20 per cent of Nigeria’s exports were coming from the Dangote Refinery, describing the development as evidence of progress beyond the country’s traditional export sources. Despite acknowledging the economic gains, the former CBN governor criticised the Tinubu administration’s communication strategy, saying the government appeared to interpret criticism and constructive suggestions as attacks. “This government doesn’t express itself properly. It sees every suggestion and contribution it does not like as an attack, and it doesn’t have good spokespersons,” he said. item.title: Experts push renewables to tackle Nigeria’s power crisis
item.description: By Udeme Akpan Power sector experts have called for accelerated deployment of renewable energy and microgrids to address Nigeria’s persistent electricity supply challenges and reduce dependence on the national grid. Speaking in separate interviews with Vanguard at the recently concluded Nigeria Energy Summit in Lagos, they said decentralised power solutions would improve electricity access, particularly for businesses and rural communities. Product Manager, DEIF, Anshul Alankar, said: “The reality is that renewable energy is the in-thing, and government policy also supports it. It is important to latch on to it as early as possible, especially for the commercial sector and even for individual users. “The grid system is not able to provide all the electricity and power needed by Nigerians and Africans to maintain sustainable energy. “Nigeria has surplus solar energy, and microgrids will help because you don’t need huge infrastructure to bring power across the country. “Microgrids are a more efficient way of handling local and rural areas. You can create your own grid, minimise fuel consumption and maximise the sun, which is free.” On the growing demand for decentralised energy, he said: “We see that the need of the market is around microgrids and fuel efficiency. We provide solutions that enable batteries to work more efficiently and solar panels to be maximised.” Also speaking, Executive Director, Delmira Power Solutions, Dr. Moriam Jagun, said the company was bringing advanced power management solutions into Nigeria. She said its technologies “coordinate, protect and monitor energy, making sure that energy is efficiently generated and delivered, both for land and marine.” Sales Head, Engineering, Delmira Power Solutions, Engr. Nmecha Chizinum Ayodele, said: “Our country has come to the point of further expansion in renewable energy, from household to grid levels.” He added: “DEIF solutions can remotely monitor, automate and synchronise different power sources to provide all-round power for industries and homes, thereby reducing the cost of energy.” The post Experts push renewables to tackle Nigeria’s power crisis appeared first on Vanguard News .

item.title: US Midterm: Democrats Retake Senate In Major Blow Against Trump’s Republicans
item.description: Democrats won full control of the US Congress in a sweeping midterm rout Tuesday with a landslide of upsets that delivered a crushing rebuke of President Donald Trump and his Republican Party. The victory handed Democrats both the House of Representatives and Senate, giving them power to block Trump’s agenda and investigate alleged corruption for the last two years of his presidency. The vote reflected deep anger over living costs, tariffs and Trump’s war against Iran, which has sent fuel prices soaring and compounded dissatisfaction with an already deeply unpopular president. Trump struck a conciliatory note despite his history of questioning election results, telling The New York Times: “I am absolutely willing to accept those results” and promising to “work with the Democrats.” But minutes later on social media, the 80-year-old signaled how he intends to deal with Democratic attempts to pass laws, posting a picture of a red baseball cap emblazoned: “VETO.” The Democrats’ decisive Senate breakthroughs came in Kansas and Iowa, the fifth and sixth Republican-held seats to fall in the extraordinary “blue wave” election night. In Kansas, Methodist minister Adam Hamilton defeated Republican incumbent Roger Marshall, becoming the first Democrat elected to the Senate from the reliably conservative state since 1932. Iowa had not elected a Democratic senator since 2008, again illustrating the scale of the party’s inroads into Republican strongholds. The upsets followed victories in Texas, South Carolina, North Carolina and Ohio, where voters rejected Republican candidates despite Trump’s intensive efforts to rally his supporters. Texas was a political bombshell. Democrat James Talarico ousted a Trump-backed Senate candidate, while Gina Hinojosa unseated Republican governor Greg Abbott, ending decades of Republican control of the state’s top office. Democrats also protected key Senate seats of their own, including Jon Ossoff’s in Georgia and an open seat in New Hampshire. Republicans had held a 53-47 Senate majority. The six-seat Democratic gain proved sufficient for networks to project a takeover despite some races remaining unresolved. Supporters of Democratic US Senate candidate James Talarico cheer after he won the Texas race during a midterm election night watch party at the Long Center for the Performing Arts in Austin, Texas, on November 3, 2026. Republican Heartland Democrats also captured the House after flipping Republican-held districts in states stretching from Pennsylvania and New Jersey to Kentucky, Arizona and North Carolina. Some victories came in territory Trump had carried comfortably in 2024, despite Republican attempts to shore up House seats by redrawing electoral boundaries. One bellwether was Indiana, where Democrat J.D. Ford defeated Republican congresswoman Victoria Spartz in a district Trump won by 17 points. item.title: Nigeria’s high production costs threaten industrial competitiveness — Feese
item.description: By Favour Ulebor, Abuja The Nigeria Economic Summit Group has warned that high production costs, unreliable electricity and poor logistics infrastructure are undermining Nigeria’s industrial competitiveness, calling for a council within the Presidency to coordinate industrialisation policies. Co-facilitator of the NESG, Lumun Feese, said Nigeria needed a coordinated approach to industrial development to address structural challenges and enable local manufacturers to compete effectively in African markets. She spoke at a breakout session on building an integrated industrial ecosystem during the 32nd Nigeria Economic Summit on Tuesday in Abuja. Feese said Nigeria had dropped from eighth to 14th position on the African Development Bank’s Africa Industrialisation Index, although she noted that the methodology had changed and more countries had been included in the latest ranking. She said, “We are not maximising our potential and our large economy. “How do we go and compete in South Africa when our cost of production is so high? Power, logistics and so on and so forth.” She added that Nigeria needed to move beyond its domestic market and develop the capacity to supply other African countries. Feese said the proposed industrialisation, competitiveness and regional integration council would provide a central coordinating platform within the Presidency to align government policies, improve implementation of the National Industrial Policy and strengthen private-sector participation. She said Nigerian businesses needed reliable power, efficient transportation systems and lower production costs to take advantage of the African Continental Free Trade Area, which offers access to a wider continental market. Feese said the recommendations followed consultations on mining, the blue economy, power, oil and gas, and industrial competitiveness. She urged businesses and other stakeholders to sustain their engagement with the NESG’s Industrial Policy Commission, saying coordinated policies and consistent implementation were necessary to achieve measurable industrial growth. item.title: ADC vows to proceed with Sokoto campaign despite intimidation
item.description: The African Democratic Congress (ADC) has vowed to proceed with its scheduled campaign in Sokoto State despite what it described as attempts by the state government to intimidate the opposition and obstruct its political activities. The party also warned that Governor Ahmed Aliyu would be held responsible if any violence was directed at opposition members or supporters in the state. The ADC National Publicity Secretary, Bolaji Abdullahi, stated this in a statement issued on Tuesday, accusing the Sokoto State Government of undermining democratic rights and deliberately frustrating the party’s activities ahead of the 2027 general elections. Abdullahi said the party would not be deterred by the alleged intimidation, insisting that no governor had the authority to prevent any political party from campaigning or presenting its candidates to voters. “The Sokoto State Government must understand that governing a state does not confer ownership. Public office is a temporary mandate from the people, not a licence to suppress political competition,” the statement read. “No governor has the power to decide which party can campaign, which candidate can speak, or which political choices the people of Sokoto are allowed to consider.” The ADC spokesperson called on the state government to immediately stop what he described as efforts to frustrate its lawful political activities and guarantee a level playing field for all political parties. He also reminded security agencies and other public institutions that their responsibility was to the Constitution and the Nigerian people, rather than the political interests of the ruling party. Abdullahi warned that public officials who abused their authority to obstruct lawful political activities would face the legal consequences of their actions. “Let there be no misunderstanding. The ADC will campaign in Sokoto State. We will not be intimidated, obstructed or pushed out of any part of Nigeria simply because those in power are afraid of political competition,” he said. He maintained that democratic participation was a constitutional right and not a privilege to be granted by elected public officials. The ADC spokesperson further accused the ruling party of displaying intolerance towards opposition activities, challenging it to submit itself to an open contest if it believed it had performed well in government. item.title: Petrol hits N1,370/litre as depot prices rise
item.description: By Udeme Akpan The pump price of Premium Motor Spirit (PMS), popularly known as petrol, has risen to N1,370 per litre in Lagos, following fresh increases in depot prices across major supply locations. Checks by Vanguard on Tuesday showed that MRS and NNPC filling stations sold petrol at N1,360 per litre, while Mobil sold at N1,349. Some independent marketers sold at between N1,365 and N1,370, depending on location. The increase followed sharp movements in depot prices, particularly in Lagos, where A.A. Rano raised its PMS price by N75 to N1,295 per litre, while African Terminal, Aiteo and Integrated increased their prices to about N1,300. NIPCO also raised its price by N55 to N1,305, while Dangote’s price edged up by N3 to N1,303. MRS retained its depot price at N1,310. In Port Harcourt, Matrix increased its PMS price by N15 to N1,300 per litre, while Bulk Strategic, Masters and T.S.L remained at N1,300. Warri also recorded increases, with A.Y.M. Shafa and Matrix raising their prices by N17 each to N1,300, while Parker moved up by N15 to the same level. Calabar recorded higher PMS prices, with Fynefield and Northwest at N1,360 per litre. Meanwhile, Automotive Gas Oil (AGO), or diesel, recorded mixed movements. In Lagos, WOSBAB cut its AGO price by N21 to N1,809 per litre, while Bulk Strategic reduced its price by N15 to N1,835. Rain Oil and Dangote also reduced their prices to N1,850 and N1,823 respectively. In Warri, Matrix and Rain Oil cut their AGO prices by N5 each to N1,835 per litre, while Edo Refinery, NIPCO and Prudent retained theirs at N1,840. item.title: NIMASA threatens sanctions over missing marine incident reports
item.description: By Godwin Oritse The Nigerian Maritime Administration and Safety Agency (NIMASA) has threatened sanctions against Port Facility Security Officers (PFSOs) who fail to properly report marine security incidents, warning that bypassing approved reporting channels constitutes a breach of international port security rules. The warning followed concerns that incident reports from port facilities were being sent to individual NIMASA officials instead of the agency’s designated International Ship and Port Facility Security (ISPS) Unit. In a notice signed by Mudi Isa, Head, ISPS Code Unit, the agency directed all PFSOs to route incident reports through the approved ISPS Unit email address. The notice, titled “Non-Receipt of Incident Reports/Submission to Approved ISPS Unit,” said: “It has come to our attention that the Unit is currently not receiving your incident report emails, which poses a significant risk.” NIMASA warned that the failure to use the prescribed channel could have serious implications for maritime security. “Failure to report security incidents to the correct channels constitutes a breach of ISPS compliance,” it stated. The agency specifically directed port facility security personnel to stop sending or copying reports to individual NIMASA staff emails unless expressly authorised. “Do not copy or send reports to individual staff emails unless explicitly authorised,” the notice stated. NIMASA also directed PFSOs to confirm receipt of every incident report and contact the ISPS Unit immediately if no acknowledgement was received within 24 hours. “If you do not receive an acknowledgment from the ISPS Unit within 24hrs of submission, contact the Unit immediately via phone,” it said. The agency further advised operators who were unsure of the approved reporting directory to contact the ISPS Unit for verification before submitting their reports. NIMASA said the directive was aimed at ensuring that security incidents and anomalies are captured promptly and handled through a coordinated response mechanism. item.title: Nigeria’s exports record 25% increase in 2yrs — NPA
item.description: By Godwin Oritse Nigeria’s exports have increased by 25 per cent in the last two years, driven by Federal Government reforms and improved collaboration with port terminal operators, the Managing Director of the Nigerian Ports Authority (NPA), Dr Abubakar Dantsoho, has said. Speaking at the ongoing Annual World Ports Conference in London, organised by the International Association of Ports and Harbours (IAPH), Dantsoho said the growth covered both oil and non-oil exports. “For us in Nigeria, the most important thing is that we are seeing growth as a result of this policy that we are taking. Statistically, the exports from Nigeria in the last two years has increased by 25 per cent. “These are exports that are not mainly only oil and gas. In manufacturing and agriculture, raw materials like cocoa and cashew, volumes have increased, and that is to the credit of the partnership between ourselves and the major terminal operators, APM Terminals,” he said. He attributed the improvement to Export Processing Terminals established by the NPA. “We have got about four of those in Nigeria where we collaborate with the terminal operators, the Nigeria Customs Service and other agencies that have a stake, so that everything regarding the processing of cargo for export is done locally,” he stated. On the African Continental Free Trade Area (AfCFTA), Dantsoho said: “Nigeria’s economy is very strong now because of our president’s reforms, which everyone can testify is attracting investors to the country.” He added that port reforms had improved operational efficiency and increased revenue. “We have experienced a lot of increase in volumes and revenue that has been generated by the ports across Nigeria. As a matter of fact, the efficiency in the ports in Nigeria is far better now than those of other West African countries,” he said. Dantsoho also disclosed that the Federal Government was investing $1 billion in expanding and modernising Apapa Port, with private-sector partnerships supporting infrastructure and technology development. item.title: US Midterms: Trump accepts midterm results, pledges to work with Democrats
item.description: United States President Donald Trump has said he is prepared to accept the outcome of the country’s midterm elections and work with Democrats, as results showed the opposition party heading towards control of both chambers of Congress. Trump made the remarks on Tuesday night during a telephone interview with The New York Times, as he monitored election results at the White House. “We’ll, you know, look forward to working with them,” he said. “We’ll probably work something out.” The President’s comments came amid major Republican losses, with Democrats making significant gains in closely contested races and threatening Republican control of Congress. Trump attributed his party’s poor performance partly to his absence from the ballot, suggesting that his participation could have changed the outcome. He also defended his decision to launch a war against Iran, describing it as a “very wise decision”. The President further said he had no regrets about endorsing Republican candidates, including South Carolina Senator Darline Graham and Texas Attorney-General Ken Paxton, who both lost their Senate bids. Speaking shortly before 10:30pm on Tuesday, Trump said he was following the election results during the interview. “I’m just looking at these results as I’m talking,” he said. Reacting to Graham’s defeat, he added: “I see that Darline lost. Wow, that’s amazing. How do you think Lindsey would have done if he ran?” He was referring to Senator Lindsey Graham, who reportedly died in July. Democrats were on course to take control of both the House of Representatives and the Senate as results continued to emerge, PUNCH Online had reported on Wednesday. A Democratic takeover of Congress would significantly alter the balance of political power in Washington, potentially subjecting Trump’s administration to increased congressional scrutiny and making it more difficult for the President to advance his legislative agenda during the remaining two years of his term. item.title: ADC accuses Sokoto govt of intimidation, demands reopening of campaign office
item.description: By Musa Ubandawaki, Sokoto The African Democratic Congress (ADC) has accused the Sokoto State Government of using the police to intimidate opposition politicians and frustrate its political activities, following the sealing of its state campaign office in Sokoto. The party demanded the immediate reopening of the premises, describing the action as illegal and an infringement on its constitutional rights ahead of the 2027 general elections. In a statement issued on Wednesday, the ADC said its campaign office along Ahmadu Bello Way in Sokoto metropolis was sealed on Tuesday, November 3, by officers of the Sokoto State Police Command allegedly acting on the orders of the state government. The development occurred barely hours before the commencement of the party’s presidential campaign flag-off in the state, with the proposed campaign venue reportedly remaining locked. The statement was signed by Yusuf Suleiman, also known as Dan Amar Sokoto, Deputy Director-General of Administration of the Atiku Abubakar ADC 2027 Presidential Campaign Council, and made available to journalists. The party alleged that the premises were sealed without a court order, prior notice or any lawful explanation from the authorities. It described the action as “illegal, unconstitutional and reckless”, arguing that it violated its rights to freedom of association, peaceful assembly and political participation. The ADC also cited Section 95 of the Electoral Act 2026, arguing that the action undermined the legal protections available to registered political parties to organise and conduct their activities without unlawful interference. The party further linked the development to what it described as a pattern of political intimidation in the state, recalling an alleged attack on its governorship candidate, Manir Muhammad Dan’iya, at Sultan Sadiq Abubakar International Airport four days earlier. It dismissed suggestions that the authorities might not have known who occupied the building, insisting that the party had operated openly from the premises for more than eight years. “The claim that the authorities do not know who occupies the building is not credible. The ADC has operated openly from those premises for more than eight years,” the statement said. The party argued that any genuine inquiry into the ownership or occupation of the property should have been made through a formal letter rather than the deployment of armed police officers to seal its premises. It also alleged that the state government was concerned about the growing support for the ADC and its candidates, accusing it of responding to political competition with force rather than democratic engagement. “We reject this conduct in its entirety. We will pursue every legitimate and lawful remedy available to us to reopen our office and to protect our members, our supporters and our property in Sokoto,” it stated. item.title: LG reinforces leadership in refrigerator market with Brandcom award
item.description: LG Electronics has strengthened its position in Nigeria’s home appliance market following the recognition of its MoodUP Refrigerator at the BRANDCOM awards 2026 in Lagos. The award recognises the refrigerator’s distinctive design and smart features, including customisable LED door panels and smart connectivity, which allow users to personalise their kitchen experience. Beyond its aesthetics, LG’s refrigerator range addresses practical household needs such as food preservation, energy efficiency and durability, which remain important considerations for Nigerian consumers. The company offers top-freezer, bottom-freezer, side-by-side and premium refrigerator models designed to accommodate different household sizes and lifestyles. One of its products, the GN-F452PFAQ Top Freezer Refrigerator, features FRESH Converter+ technology, which allows users to adjust temperature settings to suit different food types and maintain optimal freshness. It also comes with an automatic ice maker for added convenience. Selected LG refrigerator models are equipped with Smart Inverter Compressor , LINEARCooling and DoorCooling+ technologies, designed to improve energy efficiency, provide consistent cooling and preserve food freshness for longer. These features are particularly relevant to households seeking reliable refrigeration, lower energy consumption and dependable appliance performance. The recognition at the BRANDCOM Awards further highlights LG’s presence in Nigeria’s competitive refrigerator market. item.title: REFORMS: Oil output has grown by 600,000bpd since PIA — NNPC
item.description: By Obas Esiedesa, Abuja Nigeria’s crude oil production has increased by 600,000 barrels per day (bpd), from about 1.2 million bpd to 1.8 million bpd, following the implementation of the Petroleum Industry Act (PIA) and reforms in the oil and gas sector, the Nigerian National Petroleum Company Limited (NNPC) has said. Group Chief Executive Officer of NNPC Limited, Mr Bashir Bayo Ojulari, disclosed this yesterday at the 2026 Abu Dhabi International Petroleum Exhibition and Conference (ADIPEC) in Abu Dhabi, United Arab Emirates. Speaking at an Energy Talk titled, “Nigeria’s Reform Agenda: Competing for Energy Capital,” Ojulari attributed the production increase to the implementation of the PIA 2021, improved investment climate, better investment decisions and stronger collaboration between NNPC and its partners. He said the company was working towards achieving Nigeria’s two million bpd production ambition by 2027 through improved maintenance of existing infrastructure, protection of base production, increased output from producing assets and execution of new projects. “The figure of 1.8 million barrels per day is a stage in a journey towards our objective. We are concentrating on the basics, which are maintaining our infrastructure, protecting base operations and executing the projects that will take production higher,” he said. On domestic energy supply, the NNPC boss said the removal of petrol subsidy had been accompanied by a major compressed natural gas (CNG) programme, with more than 400 conversion centres established across the country. He added that over 1,000 trucks used in transporting petroleum products had also been converted to run on CNG. Ojulari disclosed that the Obiafu-Obrikom-Oben (OB3) gas pipeline was completed in August 2026, while the Ajaokuta-Kaduna-Kano (AKK) pipeline was expected to deliver gas to Abuja before the end of the year to support power generation, data centres and industrial hubs. On gas development, he said NNPC was targeting national production of 10 billion standard cubic feet per day (Bscf/d) by 2027 and 12 Bscf/d by 2030, supported by the development of domestic and international markets. He also said the countries involved in the Nigeria-Morocco Gas Pipeline had aligned and executed the necessary agreements, while Nigeria, Algeria and Niger had reached alignment on the development of the Trans-Saharan Gas Pipeline. On investment, Ojulari cited major projects, including TotalEnergies’ Ubeta, Shell’s Bonga South-West and Eni’s Zabazaba developments, noting that commercial agreements covering about $20 billion in investments had been concluded. He added that NNPC was building new relationships with international partners, including the Abu Dhabi National Oil Company (ADNOC) and Chinese investors in Nigeria’s refineries, while working with global oilfield service companies to expand capacity in the country. item.title: ADC’s struggle to campaign
item.description: There was an air of uncertainty on Tuesday over whether the flag-off of the African Democratic Congress (ADC) presidential campaign in Sokoto State scheduled for Wednesday (today) would be held as planned. Daily Trust gathered that, as of Tuesday evening, the party was still struggling to secure a venue for the event, mobilise supporters, and make other basic logistical arrangements for the rally. Our correspondents report that the event was initially scheduled for Saturday, October 31, but was shifted to Wednesday due to the alleged takeover of hotel bookings by the state government, which has denied the claim. It was learnt that due to problems of logistics, some ADC leaders in the state offered their homes and guest houses to accommodate party leaders and other dignitaries arriving for the party’s presidential campaign flag-off. Benue APC: Rival Tinubu campaign lists deepen factional rift Can the North afford to continue without its own ‘Parapo’? Some party leaders confirmed this in separate interviews with our correspondents, saying they resorted to providing private accommodation after failing to secure hotel rooms for their guests. Spokesman for the ADC governorship candidate in Sokoto State, Aminu Abubakar, said the party was yet to secure hotel accommodation, prompting members to volunteer their residences and guest houses. “Some of them have offered their homes, while others have provided their guest houses to accommodate our visitors. That is where we are putting them up,” he said. Another party chieftain, who spoke on condition of anonymity, said some prominent party leaders had already arrived in Sokoto ahead of the event. He said they include the party’s National Secretary and former Osun State Governor, Rauf Aregbesola; Senator Dino Melaye; and the party’s governorship candidate in Kaduna State, Isa Ashiru Kudan. The source added that more party leaders and dignitaries were expected to arrive Tuesday night or early Wednesday. However, the party was yet to officially announce the exact venue of the rally as of the time of filing this report. A source familiar with the arrangement alleged that the party had been asked to pay N20 million for the use of the Trade Fair Complex. According to the source, the party had agreed to the payment and requested the account details to enable it to transfer the money, but the details had yet to be provided. Director-General of the ADC Governorship Campaign Council, Bello Muhammad Goronyo, when contacted for clarification on the arrival of party leaders and the venue of the event declined to comment, saying he was not aware of the arrival of the guests or where the presidential campaign flag-off would take place. item.title: Inter End Champions League Slump With 3-0 Win Over Feyenoord
item.description: Inter Milan got their stuttering Champions League campaign back on track with a comfortable 3-0 win Tuesday against Dutch giants Feyenoord, helped by a superb first-half strike from German defender Yann Bisseck. The three-time champions of Europe had lost their first two group games, but had far too much quality for a disappointing Feyenoord, who had little answer to Inter’s pace and attacking ability. On a clear and crisp evening in Rotterdam, the visitors quickly silenced the ever raucous crowd in De Kuip, piling on sustained pressure that paid dividends as early as the eighth minute. Bisseck was given too much space on the edge of the box, allowed to turn and drill a sumptuous curling left-footed shot low past the diving Tjark Ernst in the Feyenoord goal. Feyenoord struggled to break out of the Inter Milan high press and the Serie A champions dominated possession and territory for much of the first quarter. The home fans had to wait for half an hour before their side produced their first effort of note, a clever one-two playing in Anis Hadj Moussa, who saw his shot blocked. And Inter doubled their advantage shortly afterwards. Feyenoord’s Dutch midfielder #10 Luciano Valente (R) reacts at the end of the the UEFA Champions League, league phase, Matchday 4, football match between Feyenoord and Inter Milan at De Kuip Stadium in Rotterdam on November 3, 2026. (Photo by JOHN THYS / AFP) England international Djed Spence found himself in acres of space on the right hand side. His shot looped up off a defender, allowing Pio Esposito to bundle in with his head from short range. The beginning of the second half brought more misery for Giovanni van Bronckhorst’s men, as Feyenoord’s defence backed off and invited an advancing Piotr Zielinski to shoot. The Polish international midfielder gratefully accepted the invitation, firing home an unstoppable drive off the post on 54 minutes. With the game effectively over as a contest, Inter boss Cristian Chivu rang the changes, bringing off star striker Marcus Thuram. Halfway through the second half, fireworks launched from outside the stadium landed on the pitch and roof, causing a short interruption. And the match itself rather fizzled out, as Inter cruised and Feyenoord failed to find any spark to penetrate the Italian defences. The win saw Inter climb to a more respectable place in the middle of the Champions League table while Feyenoord’s solitary victory leaves them adrift of the knock-out phase. Feyenoord’s next Champions League encounter is a home tie against Porto, while Inter Milan welcome Stuttgart. item.title: Raphinha, Yamal Fire Barcelona To Champions League Win Over Villa
item.description: Raphinha struck twice to propel Barcelona to a 3-0 Champions League win over visitors Aston Villa on Tuesday, ending the English side’s perfect start to the competition. Five-time winners Barcelona took an early lead through Lamine Yamal before Raphinha continued his fine goalscoring form with a second-half brace. Barca bounced back after defeat by champions Paris Saint-Germain in their previous European outing to stay in the hunt for a top eight league phase berth. Unai Emery’s Villa competed well in the first half but were eventually undone by Barca’s greater ability in the final third. The Champions League anthem was not played before the game, as a mark of respect for Tenerife striker Jesus De Miguel, who died on Tuesday morning after an on-pitch collision in a Spanish second division match the previous day, provoking shock across the football world. Villa captain John McGinn had only visited the Camp Nou once previously, on a summer holiday as an eight-year-old, and might have expected better weather than the downpour both teams were subjected to. The skipper might also have expected a more focused start, with Villa handing Barcelona the lead in the seventh minute. Barcelona’s Spanish forward #10 Lamine Yamal (R) and Barcelona’s English forward #17 Anthony Gordon fight for the ball with Aston Villa’s Dutch defender #22 Ian Maatsen (L) and Aston Villa’s Swedish defender #03 Victor Lindelof during the UEFA Champions League 1st round day 4 football match between FC Barcelona and Aston Villa at Camp Nou Stadium in Barcelona on November 3, 2026. (Photo by MANAURE QUINTERO / AFP) The Spanish champions pressed Aston Villa extremely high and Joao Gomes played a poor pass straight to Yamal in his own box. The 19-year-old winger gladly took the gift and stroked past Villa goalkeeper Zion Suzuki. Villa reacted strongly and Matty Cash had a vicious drive deflected narrowly wide before Joao Cancelo blocked Gomes’s effort. Barcelona goalkeeper Joan Garcia was quick off his line to beat Nicolas Jackson to a dangerous through-ball. Suzuki saved from Anthony Gordon as Villa again struggled to bring the ball out from the back under Barca’s pressing. Garcia was called into action again by Johan Manzambi as the match lurched from end-to-end. Barcelona extended their lead early in the second half when Fermin Lopez fed Raphinha, who showed quick footwork before finding the bottom corner. Cancelo powered a strike narrowly over before setting up Raphinha for Barcelona’s third with a superb cross with the outside of his boot. The Brazil winger, who has made the number nine position his own this season, pounced from close range for his 19th goal of the season across all competitions. Yamal sent a shot skidding wide as Barcelona probed for a fourth. It did not come, but the Catalan giants were able to record a first Champions League clean sheet in 19 games.
